'''New Foundations consistency machines''' are binary Turing machines constructed to search for contradictions in [[Logical independence#New Foundations (NF)|New Foundations (NF)]] and two extensions: NF with Rosser's full Axiom of Counting (AxCount), and NF with the full Cantorian Sets principle (CS).

The latest constructions in the R. Gutin and E. Glazer reduction series have '''173''', '''182''' and '''197 working states''', respectively. These counts include blank-tape initialization, the proof-search decoder, arithmetic and return control. The terminal halt state is separate and is not included in the count. The release documentation distinguishes the checked implementations from the inherited logical calibrations.<ref name="nf173">R. Gutin and E. Glazer, [https://github.com/wlad-svennik/notes/tree/main/nf-bb173 ''Pure NF: a 173-state binary machine''], 25 November 2026. Includes the literal table, portable verification archive and proof-scope notes.</ref><ref name="count182">R. Gutin and E. Glazer, [https://github.com/wlad-svennik/notes/tree/main/nf-axcount-bb182 ''NF + full AxCount: 182-state binary machine''], 25 November 2026. Includes the literal table, portable verification archive and calibration audit.</ref><ref name="cs197">R. Gutin and E. Glazer, [https://github.com/wlad-svennik/notes/tree/main/nf-cs-bb197 ''NF + CS: a 197-state binary Turing machine''], certificate dated 24 November 2026. Includes the literal table, portable phase certificate and inherited calibration notes.</ref>

These are the smallest verified implementations in the cited reduction series. No proof of global minimality is claimed. Each table is a complete deterministic machine over symbols <code>0</code> and <code>1</code>, on a two-way infinite tape initially filled with <code>0</code>. Each working state has one transition for each read symbol.

== Construction and verification ==

The implementations use the register-machine architecture developed by Andrew J. Wade: nine natural-number counters are represented in unary on a binary tape. Their instruction language uses increment, conditional decrement and structured control flow. The reductions preserve the proof-enumeration sources and use invariants at complete source operations to justify sharing physical states. They do not identify the redirected states on arbitrary tapes.

* '''NF, 173 states:''' the reduction removes one state from the supplied 174-state predecessor without changing its 2,976-site source or adding Counting. The archive supplies 3,932 unbounded physical proof domains, 20 pumping laws, 16 arithmetic induction theorems and the complete 67,998-transition blank startup. It includes standalone Lean-kernel replay of the physical, arithmetic and startup certificates.<ref name="nf173" />
* '''NF + AxCount, 182 states:''' the reduction removes one state from the supplied 183-state predecessor while retaining its 3,397-site source. The archive supplies 4,485 unbounded physical proof domains, 20 pumping laws, 16 arithmetic induction theorems and the complete 67,998-transition blank startup, with standalone Lean-kernel replay.<ref name="count182" />
* '''NF + CS, 197 states:''' the reduction removes one state from the 198-state implementation. Its portable checker covers 5,605 ordinary natural-input domains and 145 guarded phase domains, using 20 pumping laws and a 72,014-transition blank startup. Universal phase contracts compose with source invariants and a written induction over complete transfer loops.<ref name="cs197" />

The unbounded domain checks are symbolic arguments over arbitrary natural register values, rather than only execution tests at small counter values. The publication directories include reproduction commands, exact table hashes and verification receipts.

== Target theories and calibration ==

AxCount is full Rosser Counting, <math>T(n)=n</math> for every internal Frege natural number <math>n</math>; it is not restricted to externally standard numerals. Here <math>T(|A|)=|\{\{x\}:x\in A\}|</math>.

CS asserts that '''every Cantorian set is strongly Cantorian'''. A set <math>A</math> is Cantorian when <math>|A|=T(|A|)</math>, and strongly Cantorian when its singleton map <math>x\mapsto\{x\}</math> is a set. No well-orderability restriction is imposed in the CS machine.<ref name="count182" /><ref name="cs197" />

Writing <math>H_T</math> for blank-tape halting of the corresponding machine, the claimed calibration is
<math>H_T\leftrightarrow\neg\operatorname{Con}(T)</math>.
The state reductions preserve the earlier numerical refutation searches. Their logical calibration combines checked endpoints with written arguments. In particular, the NF package retains written enumeration and composition arguments; the Counting package identifies the written full-chart and numerical-calculus steps; and the CS package uses a written reverse consistency comparison from NFU with Dedekind Infinity and full CS to pure NF + CS.<ref name="nf173" /><ref name="count182" /><ref name="cs197" />

The latter comparisons are attributed to '''R. Gutin and E. Glazer, ''Choice and Consistency Strength in NF and NFU''''' in the release notes. These releases do not claim one newly completed end-to-end Lean theorem connecting the usual set-theory axioms to every step of each literal machine.

== Relation to Busy Beaver independence bounds ==

A smaller implementation is not, by itself, a new arithmetic transfer theorem. To use the 173-state machine for a PA bound by the consistency argument, one needs an argument establishing
<math>\mathrm{PA}\vdash\neg H_{173}\to\operatorname{Con}(\mathrm{PA})</math>
for that exact table. The analogous Zermelo transfer for the 182-state machine needs
<math>\mathrm{PA}\vdash\neg H_{182}\to\operatorname{Con}(Z)</math>,
together with the relevant nonhalting and consistency hypotheses. Such arguments may be ordinary mathematical proofs; they need not be packaged as a single proof-assistant theorem.

The new implementation certificates do not themselves supply those additional exact-table arithmetic implications. Accordingly, the table above records the new '''construction state counts'''; it does not independently upgrade the PA or Zermelo bounds on [[Logical independence]].
